notes:
Account summary: Avalon is a mid-stage insurtech platform handling claims ingestion and automated triage. Interested in Redwood Private (VPC) for customer data residency and to satisfy regulator audit obligations. Primary ask centers on audit logging: end-to-end export to their Splunk instance, log schema alignment, immutable retention policy, and KMS integration for log encryption.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-02-25: Security deep dive (Marcus + Riya + Avalon SecOps). Reviewed SOC2 pack and network diagram. Action: provide SIEM mapping + sample event stream.
- 2026-02-10: POC kickoff (ff-20260210-avalon-sec-review). Discussed network egress policy, firewall rules, and SAML SSO.
- 2026-01-20: Intro + use-case call; confirmed workloads: claims-triage, fraud-detection, doc-search.

Audit logging requirements (detailed):
- Export/Transport: must be able to push audit logs to customer SIEM using either TLS-encrypted syslog (RFC5424) or Splunk HEC (HTTPS). Support for CEF or LEEF formatting preferred. Option to drop copies to an S3 bucket (customer-owned) for long-term retention is required.
- Schema (required fields): timestamp (ISO8601), request_id, tenant_id (customer account id), user_id (internal actor or API key id), api_route, model_id/model_version, prompt_hash (SHA256), tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, decision/outcome label, response_status, error_code, backend_node, kv_cache_hit, container_id, cumulative_cost_usd. Fields should be present as flat key/value pairs to simplify SIEM indexing.
- PIi handling/redaction: logs must support configurable field-level redaction at source (masking before export) OR supported hooks for Redwood to mask PII (name, ssn, policy numbers). Avalon wants proof-of-concept of masking at the POC level.
- Retention: legal requires 7-year retention for audit trails for claims provenance. Redwood offering must allow configurable retention policies per-bucket/index with immutability (WORM) on the S3 archive or equivalent. Need lifecycle rules: hot (30d) -> warm (365d) -> archive (7y immutable).
- Access logs & admin audit: must capture admin activity (who rotated keys, who created model routes, who changed rollout policies). Admin audit events must be exported to the same SIEM feed and stored separately with higher-fidelity (full raw event).
- KMS integration: logs written to S3 must be encrypted with customer-managed keys (AWS KMS CMK). Redwood must support envelope encryption and key rotation policies; require proof that log decryption requires KMS permissions bound to Avalon IAM principals.
- Integrity & tamper-evidence: Avalon wants signed log batches (e.g., per-hour HMAC + signature) or object-level checksum metadata to detect tampering.
- Time sync and ordering: require all events contain monotonic sequence id + server timestamp (UTC). For forensic needs, ability to reconstruct causal chains across distributed nodes is important.
- Sampling/traces: support for full-trace capture for flagged incidents (on-demand 100% token capture for a 24-hour window) but default sampling at 5% for high-volume routes; sampling rate must be configurable per-route.
- Performance considerations: must ensure logging at required fidelity does not add >10ms p50 latency. Redwood to provide benchmarks for logging overhead during POC.

POC scope & success criteria:
- Deliver SIEM mapping doc + sample JSON/CEF events by 2026-03-03 (Redwood deliverable).
- End-to-end export to Avalon Splunk HEC endpoint (test index) within POC window. Validate parsing and dashboards.
- Demonstrate KMS-encrypted S3 archiving with lifecycle rules and WORM.
- Run 48-hr POC with production-ish traffic (claims ingestion) and show <10ms added latency, correct retention lifecycle, and successful admin audit export.

Quotes / paraphrase from SecOps: "We cannot accept opaque logs — we need a deterministic schema and proof of immutability for audits."-- Avalon SecOps lead.

Commercial / procurement notes: procurement prefers a 12-month committed Dedicated + Private control plane. Pricing deck shared (linked). Avalon wants a clear uplift estimate for the added cost of 7-year retention.
